title: Renewal + geo extension sync: Brightline Grocers
summary: Customer is approaching renewal window. Discussion focused on a capacity uplift for peak grocery holiday load, adding a Japan edge/on-prem pilot to reduce latency for JP stores, contract term extension options (12 vs 24 months) with committed burst blocks, and security/compliance checkpoints. SE captured preliminary perf targets to run a short dedicated throughput benchmark. Agreed next steps: send updated pricing matrix, share SOC2 + KMS docs, schedule SE-led benchmark week of 2027-01-31.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan, Maya, Liam (Redwood); Clara, Marcus, Priya, Samir (Brightline)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ethan): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today, uh again quick agenda — renewal window, capacity needs for upcoming holiday peak, and that japan edge pilot we talked about. is that about right?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Clara): yeah that's perfect, thanks. we've got some new requirements since last quarter — more store-l-level models running for receipts, checkout, and local ads, so peak is higher than we expected.
00:35 Speaker 1 (Ethan): totally, and congrats on the growth. maya i'll hand over to you to walk through what we can do for a capacity uplift and the edge option?
00:42 Speaker 3 (Maya): yeah, thanks. so quick pointer — there are two levers: 1) add dedicated GPU capacity (reserved pool) and 2) add a small private on-prem / japan edge cluster for sub-60ms round trips for JP stores. with dedicated we guarantee throughput and we can provision burst nodes for the nov holidays, uh i mean the new year promos.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): sorry interject, when you say "private on-prem" is that full air-gapped or VPC-based? we need to understand egress and keys.
01:13 Speaker 3 (Maya): good q — for the pilot we recommend VPC-mode private deployment in our partner region (tokyo region). not fully air-gapped. KMS integration for keys, and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. if you need HSM or air-gap we can scope that as a separate project.
01:32 Speaker 2 (Clara): okay makes sense. for latency targets — currently our user-facing latency budget is 120ms for JP checkouts. we want to get under 80ms ideally.
01:43 Speaker 3 (Maya): right, with a small Japan edge and model quantization we usually see 35-70ms median for the kinds of 512-token requests you're doing. caveat: depends on batch sizes and KV cache hit rates — i noticed your docs mention frequent short-lived prompts.
02:04 Speaker 5 (Samir): yeah that's true, we do a lot of single-turn short prompts, not batch. how much does that hurt cost?
02:11 Speaker 3 (Maya): single-turn hurts batching efficiency, but caching helps — automatic prefix/KV caching can reduce repeated prefix cost. there was a note about 'KV cash' earlier in last call, so i want to make sure cache hit instrumentation is enabled.
02:28 Speaker 1 (Ethan): quick Q for procurement — priya, timeline for signing if we land on a 12 vs 24 month?
02:36 Speaker 6 (Priya): we can fast-track within procurement if legal is happy; procurement approval is around two weeks after final pricing. if we do a 24mo we need finance sign-off for deferred billing options.
02:49 Speaker 4 (Marcus): also, can we get a failover plan? in APAC we need a regional fallback so that if edge fails requests go to our dedicated pool in us-west with acceptable latency limits.
03:01 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes — smart routing policy can route by geo and fall back to a compatible model variant in another region. that will add ~40-80ms on top depending on route. we'll show examples in the benchmark.
03:20 Speaker 2 (Clara): what's the estimated cost delta for the edge cluster? rough ballpark.
03:27 Speaker 1 (Ethan): i'll give the high level — for the small Japan edge pilot (reserved for peak windows) think of a +20-30% uplift over your current Dedicated monthly run-rate for the pilot nodes. exact depends on GPU class and committed hours. for 24mo discounted terms we can push that down by ~12%.
03:45 Speaker 6 (Priya): can you show that in a simple pricing matrix? we need an apples-to-apples 12 vs 24mo comparison plus burst blocks.
03:53 Speaker 1 (Ethan): absolutely — i'll send an updated matrix with committed burst blocks, e.g., baseline capacity + two burst packages (50% and 100%) and pricing lines for 12 and 24 month terms.
04:05 Speaker 5 (Samir): on security — SOC2 coverage still good right? and audit logs retention? also KMS.
04:12 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes SOC2 in the control plane; we'll share the attestation and the audit log export doc. KMS can be customer-managed keys via our KMS integration — logs can be sent to your SIEM via syslog/S3. if you need HSM-backed signing that's an add-on.
04:33 Speaker 4 (Marcus): perfect. one more technical: how do you handle KV cache warming for new models and rollouts? last time a rollout doubled latency for a few hours.
04:44 Speaker 3 (Maya): good point — we recommend staged rollouts with auto-warming using synthetic traffic; also our runtime does prioritized KV-cache seeding for pinned versions. occasionally there's a transient spike, but with canary rollout policy you can limit exposure.
05:05 Speaker 2 (Clara): we'd like to run a dedicated throughput benchmark — measure tokens/sec and p95 latency for our prompt corpus. can you run that?
05:12 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes — plan is to run it in a staged window: DAY 1 baseline on your current plan, DAY 2 dedicated pool with identical model and quant settings, DAY 3 edge pilot in tokyo. we'll need your sample prompt set and representative traffic pattern.
05:29 Speaker 6 (Priya): timeline — can the pilot happen week of Jan 31? procurement should clear the budget by then but i need confirmed dates from you.
05:36 Speaker 1 (Ethan): yes week of Jan 31 works. maya will lead ops and i'll coordinate SOW and pricing.
05:42 Speaker 3 (Maya): i'll send the benchmark plan by Tue 1/26 and propose three daily windows for the run. also will include success criteria: p95 < 120ms for edge, p95 < 200ms fallback, tokens/sec > X (we'll compute after we see your CSV).
06:00 Speaker 4 (Marcus): i will upload the last q4 token/latency CSV to the shared folder by 1/26.
06:07 Speaker 2 (Clara): on contract length: what flexibility do we have to add capacity mid-term without penalty?
06:13 Speaker 1 (Ethan): we support top-ups anytime; pricing for top-ups will be at the agreed committed rate for the term if done within the first 30 days of the quarter; otherwise pro-rated. also we can add burst blocks as an addendum.
06:29 Speaker 5 (Samir): any notes about migrating models if we change quantization or use newer variants? risk of regressions?
06:36 Speaker 3 (Maya): we have an eval harness and quality monitoring. before any quant/variant swap we run evals against your golden prompt set and a quick A/B canary. we'll set up a regression alert tied to your prompts and QoQ metric.
06:51 Speaker 2 (Clara): okay good. are there any vendor references that ran a similar japan edge?
06:57 Speaker 1 (Ethan): yeah we have a retail customer (anonymized) who did a tokyo edge pilot — saw 45% p95 latency improvement. i'll include a one-pager reference in my follow-up.
07:12 Speaker 6 (Priya): procurement question — we'd like net-60 invoices for the first year; is that doable?
07:19 Speaker 1 (Ethan): net-60 is possible with finance approval for renewals >= $X. if the deal lands at the uplifted commitment we'll escalate to finance and include net-60 in the amendment.
07:33 Speaker 4 (Marcus): last tech question — what's the expected deployment time for the edge cluster once signed?
07:39 Speaker 3 (Maya): once contract and VPC peering info is in, small pilot cluster can be provisioned in 7-14 business days; full harden + KMS integration might push to 3-4 weeks.
07:52 Speaker 2 (Clara): cool. that's all from our side. thanks.
07:56 Speaker 1 (Ethan): recap: maya sends benchmark plan by 1/26; ethan sends pricing matrix and renewal amendment options by 1/28; marcus uploads Q4 CSV by 1/26; priya confirms procurement timeline by 2/02. seeding window week of 1/31. any other items?
08:18 Speaker 6 (Priya): no, that's covered. thanks.
08:22 Speaker 3 (Maya): one note — i'll include a small appendix in the benchmark plan that shows expected unit cost per token with and without caching for your top 5 prompts.
08:35 Speaker 1 (Ethan): awesome. we'll follow up in email with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff. thanks everyone, talk soon.
08:44 Speaker 2 (Clara): thanks all, bye.

End of transcript. Note: some transcription artifacts present (speaker labels and acronyms).
